record.title: Injectivity conjecture for souped-up Lie algebras
record.statement:
Let $d4e2$ be a souped-up Lie algebra, let $F(d4e2)$ be the infinite free algebra generated by $d4e2$, and let $I(d4e2)$ be the defining ideal used to construct $V(d4e2)=F(d4e2)/I(d4e2)$. The function $N(s,t)$ specifies the relations generating $I(d4e2)$. **Injectivity conjecture.** There exists some constant $N$ such that, for any souped-up Lie algebra $d4e2$, one has

$$
I(d4e2)\capd4e2=\{0\}
$$

when $N(s,t)\equiv N$. This conjecture asserts that the generating souped-up Lie algebra survives intact in the associated vertex algebra quotient; it is proved in the basic cases treated in the paper but remains unproved for arbitrary souped-up Lie algebras.
record.source_name: Timothy Eller, “Chiral vector bundles”, arXiv:1004.3081 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3081

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2010).

record.title: MMSE transform injectivity conjecture up to reflection
record.statement:
Let $X$ and $Z$ be zero-mean random variables, and for $\rho\in[0,\infty)$ let ${\mathsf{mmse}}(X,\rho)$ denote the minimum mean-square error in estimating $X$ from a Gaussian-noise observation at signal-to-noise ratio $\rho$. **MMSE transform injectivity conjecture.** For all ${\mathsf{snr}}\in[0,\infty)$,

$$
{\mathsf{mmse}}(X,{\mathsf{snr}})={\mathsf{mmse}}(Z,{\mathsf{snr}})
$$

if and only if $X$ is identically distributed as either $Z$ or $-Z$. This asks whether the MMSE transform determines a zero-mean input distribution up to reflection; the source presents it as an interesting question that remains to be answered.
record.source_name: Dongning Guo, Yihong Wu, Shlomo Shamai and Sergio Verdu, “Estimation in Gaussian Noise: Properties of the Minimum Mean-Square Error”, arXiv:1004.3332 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3332

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2010).

record.title: Optimal first transmission conjecture for Boolean threshold functions
record.statement: Let $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be the block of Boolean observations, let $\Pi_{n-k}(X^n)$ denote the Boolean threshold function, and suppose the probability distribution satisfies $p_1\leq p_2\leq\ldots\leq p_n$. **Optimal first transmission conjecture.** In order to compute $\Pi_{n-k}(X^n)$, it is optimal for node $k+1$ to transmit first, using the Huffman code, for all $n$ and all $0\leq k\leq n-1$. The conjecture proposes an optimal ordering for block computation under arbitrary interactive strategies and zero-error computation; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Hemant Kowshik and P. R. Kumar, “Optimal ordering of transmissions for computing Boolean threhold functions”, arXiv:1004.5571 (2010).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.5571

record.title: The collapsing conjecture for twisting spectral sequences
record.statement: Let $F$ and $G$ be strict polynomial functors, and for $r\geq 0$ let $E(F,G,r)$ denote the twisting spectral sequence associated with them, whose abutment computes ${\mathrm{Ext}}^*(F^{(r)},G^{(r)})$. **Collapsing conjecture.** For all $r\geq 0$, and all $F,G$, the twisting spectral sequence $E(F,G,r)$ collapses at the second page. The conjecture would explain why known computations exhibit equality between the total dimensions of the twisted Ext groups and the corresponding second-page terms, even without an evident lacunary argument; whether this collapse always occurs remains open.
record.source_name: Antoine Touzé, “Troesch complexes and extensions of strict polynomial functors”, arXiv:1005.3133 (2011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3133

record.title: Krasikov's discrete Laguerre inequality for polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_n$ denote the real polynomials of degree $n$ with only real zeros. For such a polynomial $p$, let $\mu(p)$ be the minimum spacing between neighboring zeros. **Krasikov's conjecture.** If $p(x)\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_n$ and $\mu(p)\ge 1$, then

$$
(n-1)[p(x+1)-p(x-1)]^2-4np(x)[p(x+1)-2p(x)+p(x-1)]\ge 0
$$

for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. This discrete analogue of the classical Laguerre inequality is proved in the paper, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: George Csordas and Matthew Chasse, “Discrete analogues of the Laguerre inequalities and a conjecture of I. Krasikov”, arXiv:1005.5186 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.5186

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Continuous Hirsch Conjecture for central-path curvature
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda(n,d)$ denote the largest total curvature of a central path over polytopes defined by $n$ inequalities in dimension $d$ and over all linear objectives.

**Continuous Hirsch Conjecture.**

$$
\Lambda(n,d) \in O(n).
$$

Equivalently, there is a constant $K$ such that $\Lambda(n,d) \leq Kn$ for all $n$ and $d$.

The source explains that known lower bounds make this conjectured linear behavior asymptotically tight. Its status is not resolved in the supplied material.
record.source_name: Edward D. Kim, “Geometric Combinatorics of Transportation Polytopes and the Behavior of the Simplex Method”, arXiv:1006.2416 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2416

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2010).

record.title: Fon-der-Flaass conjecture for the Turán (3,4)-problem
record.statement:
Let $\rho_3$ denote the limiting minimum edge density for $3$-graphs without independent sets on four vertices, and let $\pi^{\mathrm{FDF}}(\rho_3)$ denote the density obtained from the Fon-der-Flaass construction.

**Fon-der-Flaass conjecture.**

$$
\pi^{\mathrm{FDF}}(\rho_3)\geq \frac{4}{9}.
$$

The paper studies the Fon-der-Flaass construction and proves the bound under additional hypotheses on the underlying graph, while improving the unrestricted bound to $7/16(1-o(1))$. The unrestricted conjectural bound remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Alexander Razborov, “On the Fon-der-Flaass Interpretation of Extremal Examples for Turan's (3,4)-problem”, arXiv:1008.4707 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.4707

record.title: Lovász's mobility–chromatic number conjecture for finite loopless graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite loopless graph. Its chromatic number is denoted by $\chi(H)$, and its mobility $m(H)$ is the largest integer $d$ for which $H$ is $d$-mobile, meaning that $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$ is connected for every finite simple graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $d-2$. **Lovász's conjecture.** For all finite loopless graphs $H$, 
$$
m(H) \leq \chi(H).
$$
 Brightwell and Winkler proved this inequality when $\chi(H)\leq 3$, and Lovász has an unpublished proof when $\chi(H)\leq 4$; the conjecture remains open in general.
record.source_name: Sukhada Fadnavis, Matthew Kahle and Francisco Martinez-Figueroa, “Warmth and mobility of random graphs”, arXiv:1009.0792 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.0792

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2010). “Brightwell and Winkler have shown this for $\chi(H) \le 3$, and Lov\'asz has an unpublished proof for $\chi(H) \le 4$ as noted in , but in general this conjecture is open.”

record.title: Equality of multiplicity bounds for polynomial and piecewise linear coefficients
record.statement:
Let $\mu_{1}(m,n)$ be the maximum multiplicity of $z=0$ when $B(t)$ and $A(t)$ are polynomial functions of degrees $m$ and $n$, respectively. Let $\mu_{2}(m,n)$ be the maximum multiplicity of $z=0$ when $B(t)$ and $A(t)$ are continuous piecewise linear functions with $m$ and $n$ segments, respectively; for $\mu_{2}$, the segments are connected at $\frac{k}{n}$ for $k=1,2,\ldots,n-1$. Consider equations (1.1) and (1.4) from the paper. **Multiplicity equality conjecture.** For the equations (1.1) and (1.4),

$$
\mu_{1}(m,n)=\mu_{2}(m,n)
$$

for all $m$ and $n$. The preceding results verify this equality for several low-degree cases, but its validity for all $m$ and $n$ remains open.
record.source_name: Mohamad Ali Alwash, “Polynomial differential equations with piecwise linear coefficients”, arXiv:1009.6019 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.6019

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

record.title: Conjecture on the facets of the network model cone
record.statement: Let $B$ denote the model matrix for the directed random graph network model with reciprocation, and let $\mathrm{cone}(B)$ be its cone. For a network on $n$ nodes, **the facets conjecture.** $\mathrm{cone}(B)$ has $3n$ facets: $2n$ correspond to patterns of zeros leading to a zero row or column margin, and the remaining $n$ correspond to patterns of zeros that cause the maximum-likelihood estimate not to exist without inducing zero margins. This conjecture is based on computations in \texttt{polymake} for networks of size up to $n=10$; a general proof is not provided in the source.
record.source_name: A. Rinaldo, S. Petrović and S. E. Fienberg, “On the Existence of the MLE for a Directed Random Graph Network Model with Reciprocation”, arXiv:1010.0745 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.0745

record.title: Rank-two conjecture for the tiny zero-sum constant
record.statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers with $m\mid n$. For a finite Abelian group $G$, let $\mathsf{t}(G)$ be the smallest integer such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\mathsf{t}(G)$ contains a non-empty zero-sum subsequence whose cross number is at most $1$. **Rank-two conjecture.** For all such $m,n$,

$$
\mathsf{t}(C_m\oplus C_n)=2m+n-2.
$$

The corresponding formula for $\eta(C_m\oplus C_n)$ is known, while the exact value of $\mathsf{t}(G)$ is known in the paper only for cyclic groups and elementary $2$-groups. The rank-two case is identified as an inviting open problem.
record.source_name: Benjamin Girard, “On a combinatorial problem of Erdos, Kleitman and Lemke”, arXiv:1010.5042 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5042

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2010). “This conjecture was proved, using tools from zero-sum theory, by Geroldinger .”

record.title: Schmeisser's strengthening of Sendov's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an $n$th-degree polynomial with $n\geq2$, let $V(F)$ be its multiset of zeros, and let $\sigma_\infty(F)$ be the radius of the smallest closed disk containing $V(F)$. Let $\operatorname{conv}(V(F))$ denote the convex hull of the zeros.

**Schmeisser's conjecture.** For every $\zeta\in\operatorname{conv}(V(F))$, the closed disk centered at $\zeta$ with radius $\sigma_\infty(F)$ contains a critical point of $F$.

This strengthens Sendov's conjecture by allowing the center to be any point in the convex hull rather than a zero of $F$. The source attributes it to Schmeisser and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Dmitry Khavinson, Rajesh Pereira, Mihai Putinar, Edward B. Saff and Serguei Shimorin, “Borcea's variance conjectures on the critical points of polynomials”, arXiv:1010.5167 (2011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

record.title: Banks–Ford–Luca conjecture on repeated values of Carmichael's function
record.statement:
Let $\lambda(n)$ be the Carmichael function, the largest order of any number modulo $n$. **Banks–Ford–Luca conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there is an integer $m\ne n$ with

$$
\lambda(m)=\lambda(n).
$$

This conjecture asserts that Carmichael's function never takes a value exactly once. The paper gives a near unconditional proof and a complete conditional proof under the Extended Riemann Hypothesis.
record.source_name: Kevin Ford and Florian Luca, “The number of solutions of lambda(x)=n”, arXiv:1010.5442 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

record.title: Conjecture on prime powers and the Pratt-tree function
record.statement:
Let $p,q,r,s$ denote primes. For a prime $q$, construct a tree $T(q)$ rooted at $q$ by linking each prime power $p^e$ exactly dividing $q-1$ to $q$, and recursively linking each $p^e$ to the prime powers $r^b$ exactly dividing $p-1$. Let $f(q)$ be the largest proper prime power occurring in $T(q)$, with $f(q)=1$ when no proper prime power occurs. **Prime-power tree conjecture.** For every prime power $p^a$, there is a prime $q$ with

$$
p^a\mid(q-1)
$$

and

$$
f(q)<p^{a+1}.
$$

This condition is intended to support the iterative argument toward the conjecture that every positive integer has another integer with the same Carmichael value; the source provides no proof or resolution of this auxiliary claim.
record.source_name: Kevin Ford and Florian Luca, “The number of solutions of lambda(x)=n”, arXiv:1010.5442 (2011).

record.title: Treglown's oriented graph analogue of Pósa's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an **oriented graph**, meaning a directed graph with no pair of opposite directed edges, on $n$ vertices. Write $\delta^+(G)$ and $\delta^-(G)$ for its minimum outdegree and indegree, respectively, and let

$$
\delta^0(G)=\min\{\delta^+(G),\delta^-(G)\}
$$

be its minimum semidegree. The **square of a Hamilton cycle** is obtained by adding an edge between every pair of vertices at distance at most two on the cycle. **Treglown's oriented graph analogue of Pósa's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(G)\geq \frac{5n}{12},
$$

then $G$ contains the square of a Hamilton cycle.

This is proposed as the oriented-graph counterpart of Pósa's square-of-a-Hamilton-cycle conjecture. The source presents it as open and gives no resolution in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Andrew Treglown, “A note on some embedding problems for oriented graphs”, arXiv:1011.4476 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

record.title: Conjectured semidegree threshold for perfect transitive-triangle packings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an oriented graph on $n$ vertices, where $3$ divides $n$. Write $\delta^0(G)$ for the minimum of the minimum outdegree and minimum indegree of $G$, and let $T_3$ denote the transitive tournament on three vertices. A **perfect $T_3$-packing** is a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $T_3$ covering all vertices of $G$. **The transitive-triangle packing conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(G)\geq \frac{7n}{18},
$$

then $G$ contains a perfect $T_3$-packing.

The source motivates this as an improvement, in terms of minimum semidegree, over Yuster's minimum-degree bound. No proof or resolution of the conjectured semidegree threshold is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Andrew Treglown, “A note on some embedding problems for oriented graphs”, arXiv:1011.4476 (2010).

record.title: Solitonic behaviour conjecture for discrete dynamical systems from general whurl relations
record.statement: The loops around the cylinder are called **whurls**, and a whurl relation is the transformation $R$ on the parameters of adjacent whurls that preserves boundary measurements. In the mixed-wires setting, the corresponding carrier action is given by tropicalizing the whurl relations, with $(+,\times)\mapsto(\min,+)$. **Solitonic behaviour conjecture.** The discrete dynamical systems arising from general whurl relations exhibit solitonic behaviour. This conjecture proposes that the box-basket-ball systems associated with whurl relations having wires in both directions retain the soliton-like dynamics known from box-ball systems with uniformly oriented wires; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Thomas Lam, Pavlo Pylyavskyy and Reiho Sakamoto, “Box-Basket-Ball Systems”, arXiv:1011.5930 (2012).

record.title: Anti-directed 2-factor conjecture for dense directed graphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a directed graph of even order $n \geq 8$, and let $\delta(D)$ denote its minimum total degree. An **anti-directed 2-factor** is a spanning 2-regular subgraph whose cycle edges, viewed as arcs of $D$, alternate in direction along each cycle.

**Anti-directed 2-factor conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(D) \geq \frac{1}{2}n,
$$

then $D$ contains an anti-directed 2-factor.

This conjecture is motivated by the paper's $\delta(D)>\frac{24}{46}n$ sufficient condition and by examples showing that the threshold cannot be lowered in general. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Ajit A. Diwan, Josh B. Frye, Michael J. Plantholt and Shailesh K. Tipnis, “A sufficient condition for the existence of an anti-directed 2-factor in a directed graph”, arXiv:1012.1231 (2011).

record.title: Limit conjecture for the largest root r_{n,m}
record.statement:
For $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $r_{n,m}$ denote the largest real root of the polynomial associated with the Bergman kernel of the Fock-Bargmann-Hartogs domain $D_{n,m}$. **Limit conjecture.** For every fixed $m\in\mathbb N$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}r_{n,m}=0.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding limit as $m\to\infty$ with $n$ fixed, but does not determine the limit in $n$; the displayed claim is supported only by numerical computation and remains open.
record.source_name: Atsushi Yamamori, “Zeros of the Bergman kernel of the Fock-Bargmann-Hartogs domain and the interlacing property”, arXiv:1101.3135 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3135

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2011). “It is already known that this conjecture is false in general (see ).”

record.title: Caro's three-quarters conjecture for rainbow connection
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices, and write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree and $rc(G)$ for its rainbow connection number. **Caro's conjecture.** If $\delta(G)\geq 3$, then

$$
rc(G)<\frac{3}{4}n.
$$

The earlier bound $rc(G)<\frac{5}{6}n$ is not expected to be optimal. The constant $3/4$ is suggested by connected 3-regular examples with $rc(G)=diam(G)=\frac{3n-10}{4}$, so the conjecture seeks a sharp universal improvement for minimum degree at least three.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Yuefang Sun, “Rainbow connections of graphs – A survey”, arXiv:1101.5747 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5747

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: The algebra-object decomposition conjecture for the _1-_3 subfactor
record.statement:
Let $N\subset M$ be the $\mathscr{I}_1$-$\mathscr{I}_3$ subfactor constructed above, and let $\gamma$ be the corresponding algebra object in $\mathscr{I}_1$. Here $\nu_j$ and $\mu_j$ denote the simple objects indexed by $j$, as in the fusion-category notation of the paper.

**Algebra-object decomposition conjecture.** The algebra object satisfies

$$
\gamma\cong 1+\sum_{j=1}^{\frac{n-1}{2}}(\nu_j+\mu_j).
$$

This conjecture identifies the algebra object associated with the constructed subfactor and would determine the corresponding principal-graph data. The paper states that it is verified in the cases $n=3$ and $n=5$, but cannot be verified for arbitrary $n$.

record.title: Subpolynomial maximal resistance in degree-two fractal mother graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G(2,m,n)$ be the finite fractal mother graph with branching parameter $m$ and level $n$, and let its maximal resistance mean the maximum effective resistance between the relevant vertices of the graph.

**Subpolynomial resistance conjecture.** The maximal resistance in $\mathcal G(2,m,n)$ grows slower than any power of $n$:

$$
\text{for every }\alpha>0,\quad R_{\max}(\mathcal G(2,m,n))=o(n^\alpha).
$$

The authors contrast this with the degree-one case and state that they will prove recurrence of $\mathcal G(2,m,\infty)$ in future work; the subpolynomial resistance assertion itself remains unproved here.

record.title: Currie–Simpson conjecture on nonrepetitive sequences modulo k
record.statement:
Let $k\geqslant 1$ be a fixed positive integer, and let $M(k)$ denote the minimum number of symbols needed to create arbitrarily long sequences whose subsequences along arithmetic progressions with common differences in $\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ are all nonrepetitive. A sequence is **nonrepetitive** if it contains no block of the form $XX$ for any nonempty finite block $X$. **Currie–Simpson conjecture.**

$$
M(k)=k+2\quad\text{for every }k\geqslant 1.
$$

The lower bound $M(k)\geqslant k+2$ is immediate, and the conjecture predicts that this bound is always attained; the case $k=1$ is Thue's theorem, namely $M(1)=3$.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Jakub Kozik and Marcin Witkowski, “Nonrepetitive sequences on arithmetic progressions”, arXiv:1102.5438 (2011).

record.title: Pattern-free sets conjecture for the six-term configuration $A_6$
record.statement:
A set of integers is **$A_6$-free** if it contains no subset of the form

$$
\{x-a-b,x-b,x-a,x+a,x+b,x+a+b\}
$$

for some $a,b>0$ with $a\neq b$. Let $r(n,A_6)$ be the maximum size of an $A_6$-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. **$A_6$-free set conjecture.** There exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
n^{3/5+\varepsilon}<r(n,A_6).
$$

Possibly $r(n,A_6)$ has order of magnitude $n^{1-o(1)}$. The conjecture seeks an improvement over the probabilistic lower bound $r(n,A_6)>\frac25 n^{3/5}$; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Borg's product conjecture for cross-intersecting hereditary families
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hereditary family, let $k\geq2$, and let $\mathcal{A}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{A}_k$ be cross-intersecting subfamilies of $\mathcal{H}$. A **largest star** $\mathcal{S}$ of $\mathcal{H}$ is a star of maximum size.

**Borg's product conjecture.** The product

$$
\prod_{i=1}^k|\mathcal{A}_i|
$$

is maximum when $\mathcal{A}_1=\cdots=\mathcal{A}_k=\mathcal{S}$ for some largest star $\mathcal{S}$ of $\mathcal{H}$.

The paper notes that the weaker sum conjecture would imply this product assertion in its range, via the arithmetic mean–geometric mean inequality, but proposes the displayed statement for every hereditary family and every $k\geq2$.

record.title: The two-part decomposition conjecture for q(k)
record.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, define

$$
q(k):=\min \sum_{i=1}^{s}\left(\omega(2k_i+1)-1\right),
$$

where the minimum is over positive integers $k_1,\ldots,k_s$ with $k_1+\cdots+k_s=k$ and $s\geq 1$, and set $q(0):=0$. Here $\omega(m)$ denotes the Ramsey number parameter used in the paper. **The two-part decomposition conjecture.** The previous statement holds with $s=2$. Even more,

$$
q(k)=\omega(2k+1)-1
$$

for all $k$ except for $k=4$. This would identify the minimum defining $q(k)$ using at most two summands, with the only exceptional value occurring at $k=4$.
record.source_name: Csaba Biró, Zoltán Füredi and Sogol Jahanbekam, “Large chromatic number and Ramsey graphs”, arXiv:1103.3917 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3917

record.title: Strong Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality for stable sheaves at minimal first Chern class
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold, let $B,\omega\in\operatorname{NS}_{\mathbb Q}(X)$ with $\omega$ ample, and let $c$ be the minimum positive value of $\omega^2\operatorname{ch}_1^B(F)$ for objects $F\in\mathcal B_{\omega,B}$. Let $E$ be a $\mu_{\omega,B}$-stable sheaf satisfying $\omega^2\operatorname{ch}_1^B(E)=c$ and

$$
\frac{\omega\operatorname{ch}_2^B(E)}{\omega^3\operatorname{ch}_0^B(E)}=\frac16.
$$

**Stable-sheaf inequality conjecture.** Then

$$
\frac{\operatorname{ch}_3^B(E)}{\omega^2\operatorname{ch}_1^B(E)}\leq\frac1{18}.
$$

This is a special case of the strong Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture for tilt-stable objects. The paper presents it as a consequence of that conjecture rather than proving it.
record.source_name: Arend Bayer, Emanuele Macri and Yukinobu Toda, “Bridgeland Stability conditions on threefolds I: Bogomolov-Gieseker type inequalities”, arXiv:1103.5010 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.5010

record.title: The Minkowski-sum formula for cluster A-varieties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a cluster $\mathcal{A}$-variety, and let $S_1,S_2$ be convex subsets of $\mathcal{A}(\mathbb{A}^t)$. For each $F\in\mathbf{E}(\mathcal{A})$, write $c_{F,S}$ for the corresponding minimum of $F^t$ on $S$. **Minkowski-sum conjecture.** The formula

$$
c_{F,S_1+S_2}=c_{F,S_1}+c_{F,S_2}
$$

holds for all cluster $\mathcal{A}$-varieties. The formula is proved in the paper for cluster $\mathcal{A}$-varieties of classical type; its validity in general is left open.
record.source_name: Linhui Shen, “Stasheff polytopes and the coordinate ring of the cluster X-variety of type A_n”, arXiv:1104.3528 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3528

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2011). “For the cluster $\mc{X}$-variety $\mc{X}_{A_n}$, the Duality Conjecture is proved in .”

record.title: The four-atom conjecture on the minimum Ingleton score
record.statement:
Given four random variables $A,B,C,D$ with a probability distribution, define the Ingleton score by

$$
\frac{I(A;B|C)+I(A;B|D)+I(C;D)-I(A;B)}{H(ABCD)}.
$$

**Four-atom conjecture.** The lowest possible Ingleton score is approximately $-0.089373$. It is attained by a four-variable distribution with alphabet size two, given by

$$
P(0,0,0,0)=P(1,1,1,1)=\alpha
$$

$$
P(0,1,0,1)=P(0,1,1,0)=0.5-\alpha,
$$

where $\alpha$ takes on a value approximately equal to $0.350457$.

This conjecture identifies a binary four-variable distribution that is claimed to minimize the Ingleton score, a normalized measure of violation of Ingleton's inequality. The parser provides no evidence resolving whether this minimum is indeed globally optimal.
record.source_name: Randall Dougherty, Chris Freiling and Kenneth Zeger, “Non-Shannon Information Inequalities in Four Random Variables”, arXiv:1104.3602 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

record.title: Treglown's conjecture for squares of Hamiltonian cycles in oriented graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an **oriented graph**, meaning a directed graph with no 2-cycles, on $n$ vertices. Let $\delta^0(G)$ denote its minimum semi-degree, the minimum of its minimum in-degree and minimum out-degree. **Treglown's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(G)\geq\frac{5n}{12},
$$

then $G$ contains the square of a hamiltonian cycle. This is an oriented-graph analogue of Pósa's conjecture, following a sufficiently-large-order oriented version of Dirac's theorem; the assertion itself is presented as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Phong Châu, Louis DeBiasio and H. A. Kierstead, “Pósa's Conjecture for graphs of order at least 210^8”, arXiv:1104.4367 (2011).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1006.0590](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0590).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.4367

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

record.title: Brouwer's 2-connectivity conjecture for strongly regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $(v,k,\lambda,\mu)$-strongly regular graph, and let $S$ be a disconnecting set of $G$ whose removal disconnects $G$ into non-singleton components. **Brouwer's conjecture.** One has

$$
|S|\geq 2k-\lambda-2.
$$

The bound $2k-\lambda-2$ is the size of the neighborhood of an edge and is therefore the natural candidate for the minimum such disconnecting-set size, denoted by $\kappa_2(G)$. The paper identifies this as Brouwer's 1996 conjecture; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioaba, Kijung Kim and Jack H. Koolen, “On a conjecture of Brouwer involving the connectivity of strongly regular graphs”, arXiv:1105.0796 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.0796

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2011). “Their work was extended recently by Brouwer and Koolen who proved the same result for distance-regular graphs thus, settling an open problem of Brouwer from .”

record.title: The logarithmic-size conjecture for p-extremal elementary graphs
record.statement:
Let $p\geq1$ be an integer. A $p$-extremal elementary graph is an elementary graph with $p$ perfect matchings and maximum possible excess $c_p$. **Elementary-graph size conjecture.** Every $p$-extremal elementary graph has at most

$$
2\log_2 p
$$

vertices. The conjecture is tight for $p=2^k$ with $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and holds for all $p\leq27$ according to the source, but its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Derrick Stolee, “Generating p-extremal graphs”, arXiv:1105.1764 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

record.title: The superadditivity conjecture for excess under factorization
record.statement:
Let $k\geq1$ and let $p,p_1,\dots,p_k$ be integers satisfying

$$
p=\prod_{i=1}^k p_i,\qquad p\geq1.
$$

Here $c_q$ denotes the maximum excess among graphs with $q$ perfect matchings. **Excess superadditivity conjecture.** For every such factorization,

$$
c_p\geq\sum_{i=1}^k c_{p_i}.
$$

The source notes that the inequality is known for all composite values discussed there in the relevant construction, but asks whether it always holds; no general resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Derrick Stolee, “Generating p-extremal graphs”, arXiv:1105.1764 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

record.title: Wójcik's extremal characterization of minimum-density union-closed families
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{F}$ be a finite union-closed family of finite sets, let $n=|\bigcup\mathscr{F}|$, and define

$$
D(\mathscr{F})=\frac{1}{n|\mathscr{F}|}\sum_{A\in\mathscr{F}}|A|,
$$

with $s_n$ the minimum of $D(\mathscr{F})$ over all union-closed families satisfying $|\bigcup\mathscr{F}|=n$. **Wójcik's extremal-family conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, any union-closed family attaining $s_n$ has the form

$$
\mathscr{F}=\{A:A\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,k\}\}\cup\{\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\},
$$

where $k=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ or $k=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$. The source presents this as an interesting question about determining $s_k$ in general; no resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Igor Balla, “Minimum density of union-closed families”, arXiv:1106.0369 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0369

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Minimum determinant conjecture for bivariate Bézier collocation submatrices
record.statement:
Let $d$ be fixed, let $\mathcal I_d$ be the set of weak $3$-compositions of $d$, and for every nonempty subset $\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d$ let $M_\Gamma$ be the corresponding Bernstein collocation matrix. Let $M_{\mathcal I_d}$ denote the full collocation matrix. **Minimum determinant conjecture.**

$$
\min_{\substack{\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d\\ \Gamma\neq\emptyset}}\det M_\Gamma=\det M_{\mathcal I_d},
$$

where the full determinant is given by the determinant formula in the source. This conjecture strengthens the positivity assertion by proposing the exact smallest determinant among all nonempty principal submatrices. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Gasper Jaklic and Tadej Kanduc, “On positivity of principal minors of bivariate Bezier collocation matrix”, arXiv:1106.0631 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0631

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Full-weight conjecture for weighted pebbling numbers of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $E(T)$ denote its edge set, and let $wp(T)$ be its weighted pebbling number. For a weighted graph, write $w_T(k)$ for the minimum total edge weight required for $T$ to achieve weighted pebbling number $k$. **Full-weight conjecture.** Every tree requires the full weight $|E(T)|/2$ to achieve its weighted pebbling number; equivalently,

$$
w_T(wp(T))=|E(T)|/2.
$$

The paper contrasts this claim with graphs such as $K_5$, where less than $|E(K_5)|/2$ can suffice, and notes that the full weight is already known to be necessary for paths, stars, and the tree considered in the preceding proposition. The conjecture asserts this necessity for all trees.
record.source_name: Stephanie Jones, Joshua D. Laison, Cameron McLeman and Kathryn Nyman, “Weighted pebbling numbers on graphs”, arXiv:1106.1625 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.1625

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Jungers–Protasov–Blondel conjecture on the overlap-free-word growth exponents
record.statement:
Let $A_1,A_2$ be the special $20\times20$ matrices with nonnegative integer entries associated with overlap-free words, and let $\mathcal{M}=\{A_1,A_2\}$. Let $\beta$ be the upper exponent of growth of the number of overlap-free binary words, and let $\rho$ denote the spectral radius. **Jungers–Protasov–Blondel conjecture.** The s.m.p. for the family $\mathcal{M}$ is $A_1A_2$, and

$$
\beta=\frac{1}{2}\log_2\rho(A_1A_2).
$$

The conjecture gives an exact value for the upper growth exponent through a spectrum-maximizing product; the paper reports only numerical bounds for $\beta$, so the assertion remains unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Nicola Guglielmi and Vladimir Protasov, “Exact computation of joint spectral characteristics of linear operators”, arXiv:1106.3755 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3755

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Conjecture on minimally knotted cycles in canonical book representations
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\widetilde{K}_n$ denote its canonical book representation. A **knotted cycle** is a cycle whose spatial embedding is a non-trivial knot, and an embedding of $K_n$ may contain knotted cycles that are not Hamiltonian.

**Minimal knotted-cycle conjecture.** The canonical book representation $\widetilde{K}_n$ contains the fewest total number of knotted cycles possible in any embedding of $K_n$.

The conjecture is motivated by computed counts for $8\leq n\leq 11$ and by lower and upper bounds for the minimum number of knotted cycles in embeddings of $K_8$; the optimality of the canonical representation remains open.
record.source_name: Andrea Politano and Dana Rowland, “Knots in the canonical book representation of complete graphs”, arXiv:1106.4065 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.4065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Heawood's empire conjecture for orientable surfaces
record.statement:
Let $S$ be an orientable surface of genus $g$, and let $h_{g,m}$ be its chromatic empire number, meaning the maximum number of colours required to colour any $m$-pire map on $S$.

**Heawood's empire conjecture.** The inequality is sharp:

$$
h_{g,m} = \left\lfloor \frac{6m + 1 + \sqrt{(6m + 1)^2 + 24(2g - 2)}}{2} \right\rfloor.
$$

This extends Heawood's conjecture for ordinary maps to empire maps on higher-genus surfaces. The source describes infinitely many unknown cases and states that a general solution remains to be found; the claim is therefore open.
record.source_name: Caspar de Haes, “Empire Maps on Surfaces”, arXiv:1106.4235 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.4235

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Borg's large-label conjecture for t-intersecting signed sets
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family, let $k\geq2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},k}$ be its signed-set family. A family has the $t$-star property if a largest $t$-intersecting subfamily is a $t$-star. **Borg's conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq1$, there exists an integer $k_0(t)$ such that for every $k\geq k_0(t)$ and every family $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},k}$ has the $t$-star property. The survey notes that the natural proposed sharp value is $k_0(t)=t+1$, based on the uniform signed-set result, but neither the general existence statement nor its sharp threshold is reported as proved.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting families of sets and permutations: a survey”, arXiv:1106.6144 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.6144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: Borg's large-label conjecture for strict t-stars of partial signed sets
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family and let $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},k}^*$ be its partial signed-set family. A family has the strict $t$-star property if every largest $t$-intersecting subfamily is a $t$-star. **Borg's conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq1$, there exists an integer $k_0^*(t)$ such that for every $k\geq k_0^*(t)$ and every family $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},k}^*$ has the strict $t$-star property. This is proposed as the partial-permutation analogue of the signed-set threshold conjecture; the survey gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting families of sets and permutations: a survey”, arXiv:1106.6144 (2011).
record.references:

record.title: The FKKR upper-bound conjecture for identifying codes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a twin-free graph, let $|V(G)|$ denote its number of vertices, and let $amma^{\text{\tiny{ID}}}(G)$ be its identifying code number. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$. **FKKR upper-bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that for every twin-free graph $G$,

$$
\gamma^{\text{\tiny{ID}}}(G) \leq |V(G)|- \frac{|V(G)|}{\Delta(G)}+c.
$$

This conjecture proposes an upper bound improving the general bound $\gamma^{\text{\tiny{ID}}}(G)\leq |V(G)|-1$ in terms of the order and maximum degree of the graph. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Florent Foucaud, Sylvain Gravier, Reza Naserasr, Aline Parreau and Petru Valicov, “Identifying codes in line graphs”, arXiv:1107.0207 (2012).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1103.3756](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3756), [arXiv:1010.5975](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5975).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.0207

record.title: The maximum number of dismal divisors in base 2
record.statement:
Let $d_2(n)$ denote the number of dismal divisors of the $k$-digit binary number $n$. **Binary maximum-divisor conjecture.** Among all $k$-digit numbers, the maximal value of $d_2(n)$ occurs at

$$
n=2^k-2=111\ldots10|_2,
$$

and this is the unique maximum except when $n=2$ or $n=4$. The conjecture is the binary counterpart of the preceding maximum-divisor claim, with explicit exceptional cases. The paper states it without a proof or resolution.
record.source_name: David Applegate, Marc LeBrun and N. J. A. Sloane, “Dismal Arithmetic”, arXiv:1107.1130 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

record.title: The two largest dismal-divisor counts among odd binary numbers
record.statement:
Let $d_2(n)$ denote the number of dismal divisors of $n$, and let $n$ range over the odd $k$-digit binary numbers. **Odd-binary divisor-count conjecture.** The unique maximum of $d_2(n)$ occurs at

$$
n=2^k-1=111\ldots111|_2.
$$

If $k\geq 3$ and $k\neq 5$, the second-largest value occurs at

$$
n=2^k-3=111\ldots101|_2,
$$

and

$$
n=2^k-2^{k-2}-1=101\ldots111|_2,
$$

possibly together with other values of $n$. This refines the preceding binary maximum conjecture by restricting to odd numbers and specifying candidates for the second-largest value; the paper gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: David Applegate, Marc LeBrun and N. J. A. Sloane, “Dismal Arithmetic”, arXiv:1107.1130 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

record.title: The asymptotic fractional matching threshold conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $f_d(k,n)$ denote the minimum $d$-degree forcing a fractional matching of the relevant size in a $k$-uniform hypergraph, with $1\le d\le k-1$. **Fractional matching threshold conjecture.** For all $1\le d\le k-1$, 

$$
f_d(k,n)\sim \left\{1-\left(\frac{k-1}k\right)^{k-d}\right\}\binom{n-d}{k-d}.
$$

The lower bound comes from the construction $H_1(\lceil n/k\rceil)$; the claim is confirmed asymptotically when $1\le k-d\le4$, but is not established for all parameters.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Peter Frankl, Hao Huang, Vojtech Rodl, Andrzej Rucinski and Benny Sudakov, “Large matchings in uniform hypergraphs and the conjectures of Erdos and Samuels”, arXiv:1107.1219 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1219

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

record.title: The standard-example conjecture for high-dimensional posets
record.statement: A **standard example** of dimension $m$ is the poset formed by the one-element subsets and the $(m-1)$-element subsets of an $m$-element set, ordered by inclusion. **Standard-example conjecture.** For every $t<1$ sufficiently close to $1$, there exists a constant $c>0$ such that every poset with $2n$ points and dimension at least $tn$ contains a standard example of dimension $cn$. The conjecture asks whether posets whose dimension is close to the maximum possible relative to their size must contain a linearly large standard example. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Csaba Biró, “Large cliques in graphs with high chromatic number”, arXiv:1107.2630 (2011).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1103.3917](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3917).

record.title: The minimum monochromatic 4-term progression density for orders not divisible by 4
record.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $m_4({\mathbb Z}_n)$ denote the minimum proportion of monochromatic $4$-term arithmetic progressions among all $2$-colorings of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. Then

$$
\inf\{m_4({\mathbb Z}_n)\colon n\text{ is not divisible by }4\}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

**The authors' conjecture.** The upper bound $1/12$ is attained as the infimum over group orders not divisible by $4$. This complements the known lower bound $7/96$ and narrows the gap between the established lower and upper bounds; the conjecture is presented as open.
record.source_name: Linyuan Lu and Xing Peng, “Monochromatic 4-term arithmetic progressions in 2-colorings of Z_n”, arXiv:1107.2888 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.2888

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

record.title: The equality of the unrestricted and triangle-free gap sequences
record.statement:
Let ${\rm gap}(n)$ be the maximum gap among graphs on $n$ vertices, let ${\rm gap}_2(n)$ be the corresponding maximum restricted to triangle-free graphs, and let $s(t)$ and $s_2(t)$ denote the associated sequences of positions defined in the paper. **Gap-sequence equality conjecture.** For every natural number $n$ and every natural number $t$, one has

$$
{\rm gap}(n)={\rm gap}_2(n)
$$

and

$$
s(t)=s_2(t).
$$

This is stated as a slightly weaker conjecture than the assertion that every gap-extremal graph is triangle-free; the paper proves the equality almost everywhere but leaves the all-$n$ and all-$t$ claim open.
record.source_name: András Gyárfás, András Sebõ and Nicolas Trotignon, “The chromatic gap and its extremes”, arXiv:1108.3444 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.3444

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).

record.title: Ruzsa's exponential bound conjecture for the Freiman–Ruzsa theorem
record.statement:
Let $F(r,K)$ denote the smallest bound such that, for every abelian group $G$ in which every element has order at most $r$, every finite subset $A\subseteq G$ satisfying $|A+A|\leq K|A|$ is contained in a coset of a subgroup of size at most $F(r,K)|A|$. Earlier bounds and examples show that $F(r,K)$ is non-decreasing in $K$, that $F(r,1)=1$, and that $F(r,K)\geq r^{2K-O(\log K)}$. **Ruzsa's conjecture.** There exists a constant $C\geq 2$ such that

$$
F(r,K)\leq r^{CK}.
$$

This conjecture asks for an essentially optimal exponential dependence on $K$ in the torsion-group form of the Freiman–Ruzsa theorem. The source provides no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Chaim Even-Zohar, “On Sums of Generating Sets in (Z_2)^n”, arXiv:1108.4902 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.4902

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).
